# Pre-fix reopened-and-re-briefed golden fixture (fn-154, R4 upgrade compatibility)

The harder half of the upgrade story. `chart_prefix_fingerprint/` covers a chart
that was **never** reopened; this one was reopened *and* successfully re-briefed
by the **pre-fix** binary, so its live briefing carries an epoch-free fingerprint
even though the chart now has a `reopened_at`.

Generated by driving the real CLI at commit `00504e00` (flow-next 3.13.1, before
the fn-154 epoch change):

```
chart create / add-decision x2 / resolve x2
chart briefing fn-1 --proposal-file proposal-b1.json   # -> B1 final, chart done
chart reopen  fn-1 --reason "split into two specs"     # -> open, B1 stale
chart briefing fn-1 --proposal-file proposal-b2.json   # -> B2 final, chart done
```

`expected.json` records both stored fingerprints (both epoch-free) and which
briefing is live.

**What it proves.** After the upgrade, the epoch-aware fingerprint of
`proposal-b2.json` no longer equals B2's stored hash. Without a legacy-hash
fallback the identical retry would find no match and die on the now-`done` chart
with `chart_not_open` - a valid, current briefing made unreachable purely by
upgrading the binary. The test asserts the retry still no-ops to B2.

It also pins the other direction: retrying `proposal-b1.json` matches **stale**
B1's legacy hash, and that must NOT be echoed back (fn-154 R6). The legacy
fallback accepts only a NON-stale match - and because every reopen stales every
briefing, a non-stale briefing can only have been minted in the current epoch.

**Do not regenerate.** These bytes are the evidence: a fixture rewritten by the
current binary would store epoch-aware hashes and quietly stop testing the
upgrade path.
